authors.aff: Professor and preacher at Basel

authors.aff: Professor of theology, Bern

authors.aff: Antistes of the Zurich church; Archdeacon at the Grossmünster
authors.sig: The library holds his homily series on Ruth, Ezra, and Nehemiah, which expound the Old Testament histories for the church while arguing against Papists, Anabaptists, and idolatry, and treating worship, the civil magistrate, and providence.

authors.aff: Professor of theology, Carolinum, Zürich
authors.sig: His De Aeterno Dei Filio (Zurich, 1568) is a substantial exegetical and polemical defense of the Son's eternal generation and consubstantiality, directed against Arians, Servetus, Gentilis, and other antitrinitarians — a document of Zurich's anti-antitrinitarian campaign.
w: On the Eternal Son of God, Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ

authors.aff: Pastor and professor at Geneva; later professor of theology at Leiden, then at the academies of Ghent, Orthez, Lescar, and Castres

authors.sig: A founding architect of French Reformed church order and confession who helped inaugurate Reformed scholastic method, bridging Calvin's generation and later Protestant orthodoxy.

authors.aff: University of Heidelberg (Collegium Sapientiae; professor of dogmatics); later the Casimirianum, Neustadt an der Haardt

authors.aff: University of Heidelberg; later rector of Herborn Academy

authors.aff: Born and died in Danzig (Gdańsk); educated at Wittenberg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg, where he taught (deputizing in Hebrew/philosophy); from 1602 professor of philosophy at the Gymnasium Academicum in Danzig
authors.sig: A pioneering Reformed systematizer whose discipline-by-discipline "systema" textbooks shaped Protestant scholastic pedagogy across early-seventeenth-century Europe.

authors.aff: Prof. of Theology, Die (1608–1629); Prof. of Theology, Edinburgh (1630–1648)
authors.sig: The library holds his Cursus theologicus (Geneva, 1620), a systematic treatment of the faith-dogma controversies with Rome ('inter nos & Pontificios'), structured largely as responses to Robert Bellarmine across loci including the church, scripture, justification, and the sacraments.

authors.aff: Rector and chair of theology, Gymnasium Illustre, Bremen
authors.sig: The works held here show him as a systematic Reformed dogmatician: a method of theology and an exposition of the Apostles' Creed treating Christology, sin, justification, grace, and last things against Roman Catholic opponents.
w: Christian and Catholic Faith (Exposition of the Apostles' Creed)

authors.aff: Professor of theology, University of Leiden; formerly pastor at Koudekerke and Middelburg, Zeeland
authors.sig: A leading architect of Dort-era Dutch Reformed orthodoxy whose co-authored Synopsis Purioris Theologiae became a standard textbook of seventeenth-century Calvinist dogmatics.

authors.aff: Preacher at Leiden; scribe of the Synod of Dort
authors.sig: The work held here is his LXX Disputationes Theologicae adversus Pontificios (1614), seventy disputations directed chiefly against the Papists and against Robert Bellarmine, treating the Church, sacraments, worship, justification, faith, and Scripture in scholastic question-and-response form.
w: Seventy Theological Disputations against the Papists

authors.aff: Regent/director of the States-General theological college at Leiden (c. 1614–1619)
authors.sig: The works here show him as an erudite Reformed controversialist: the Oxford Theses treat baptism as the covenant sign succeeding circumcision against Pelagians, Papists and Socinus, while the Responsio answers Hermann Ravensperger.

authors.aff: University of Heidelberg (professor of dogmatics; director of the Collegium Sapientiae) and later University of Groningen (professor of theology)
authors.sig: A leading exponent of Palatine Reformed orthodoxy who taught at Heidelberg and Groningen, sat at the Synod of Dort, and whose collected Heidelberg theological writings transmitted the moderate Calvinism of the Palatinate.

authors.aff: Dutch Republic; studied at Leiden; jurist and statesman (Advocate-Fiscal, Pensionary of Rotterdam); later Swedish ambassador to France in Paris
authors.sig: A foundational figure of modern international law and a pioneer of historical-philological biblical criticism, whose irenic Scripture annotations exerted lasting influence on early-modern exegesis.

authors.aff: Gymnasium Illustre (Schola Bremensis), Bremen; professor of theology and philosophy; Pastor Primarius of the Church of Our Lady

authors.sig: A leading German Reformed controversial theologian of the Thirty Years' War era, remembered chiefly for his sustained refutation of the Jesuit Martin Becanus in the Anti-Becanus.

authors.aff: Dutch Reformed minister at Leiden; regent (governor) of the Walloon College, University of Leiden
authors.sig: A pioneering Leiden orientalist whose comparative Semitic philology placed the textual criticism of Scripture on a broader Eastern-versions footing, crystallized in his posthumous Critica Sacra.

authors.full: Johannes Piscator; Ludwig Lucius; Thomas Gataker
authors.d: disputes of Piscator, Lucius and Gataker
w: Some Adversaria Writings on the Meritorious Cause of Justification

authors.aff: Reformed minister and historian; pastor at Houdan; later professor of history at the Athenaeum Illustre, Amsterdam (succeeding Vossius)
authors.sig: A leading Huguenot historian whose critical exposure of forged decretals and papal legends made him a key figure in Reformed anti-Roman controversial scholarship.
w: On the Primacy in the Church

authors.aff: Professor of theology and rector at the Viadrina, Frankfurt an der Oder; later theology professor and co-rector at the Akademisches Gymnasium and preacher at St. Ansgarii, Bremen
authors.sig: An irenic German Reformed theologian and rector of the Viadrina, whose Praxis Catholica gave classical expression to seventeenth-century efforts at Protestant Christian union.

Disputation against the Tradition of the Latins concerning the Object of Religious Worship
Exposition of the Epistle to the Philippians

authors.aff: Pastor of the Reformed church of Charenton, near Paris
authors.sig: He produced one of the most comprehensive Reformed patristic refutations of transubstantiation, a standard reference work in seventeenth-century eucharistic controversy.
w: On the Sacrament of the Eucharist

authors.aff: Professor, Academy of Saumur
authors.sig: The works held here show the range behind his reputation: a defense of predestination against its misreadings, an apologetic against religious indifferentism, polemics against Curcellaeus on the Trinity, and moral theology grounded in imitation of divine clemency.
w: Brief Treatise on Predestination and Its Principal Dependencies
Christian Ethics (La Morale Chrestienne à Monsieur de Villarnoul, Seconde Partie)
On the Elevation of Faith and the Abasement of Reason
On the Mystery of the Trinity

authors.aff: Professor of philosophy and theology at the Geneva Academy, later professor of theology at the University of Deventer and at Franeker
authors.sig: An early Reformed scholastic notable for his systematic defense of the necessity and proper use of reason and philosophy in resolving theological controversies, while polemicizing against Socinians and Arminians.
w: The Secrets of Arminianism: Two Books
The Theological Rationale, or On the Necessity and True Use of the Principles of Reason and Philosophy in Theological Controversies
Theological Rationale, or On the Necessity and True Use of the Principles of Reason and Philosophy in Theological Controversies

authors.aff: Pastor at Leiden; professor of theology at Leiden (1648–1676)
w: On the Origin of Error, Eight Books

authors.aff: Reformed pastor at Blois (Loir-et-Cher), France
authors.sig: Testard was, with Moïse Amyraut, a founding exponent of the Cameronian "hypothetical universalism" (Amyraldianism) that provoked one of the central intra-Reformed controversies of seventeenth-century France.
w: Eirenikon or Synopsis of the Doctrine on Nature and Grace (Blois 1633)

authors.aff: Professor of theology, University of Groningen (1643-1673); earlier Academy of Sedan, and pastor/professor at Maastricht and 's-Hertogenbosch
authors.sig: A leading defender of seventeenth-century Reformed scholastic orthodoxy whose Groningen Systema served as a standard dogmatics textbook while he combated Catholic, Socinian, Arminian, Cartesian, and Cocceian opponents alike.

authors.aff: Professor of philosophy at Orange, Nîmes, and Geneva
authors.sig: The Philosophia Contracta held here is his compressed philosophical course: scholastic in form (definition, proof, distinction, objection), grounded in Aristotle's principles yet arguing against Aristotelians, Copernicans, and Papists, with heavy weight on creation, anthropology, and free will — a window into Reformed philosophy at the moment atomism met Calvinist theology.

authors.aff: Academy of Geneva (professor of philosophy, then theology, rector); University of Leiden (professor of theology)
authors.sig: A leading mid-seventeenth-century Reformed scholastic who, from chairs at Geneva and Leiden, became one of the principal opponents of Amyraldism and a staunch defender of orthodox Calvinist predestination.
w: Theological Disputations, Miscellaneous, Parts One and Two

authors.aff: Minister at All Saints North Street, York
authors.sig: The two volumes held here are his annotations on Genesis and Exodus, which read the Pentateuch through the Targums and rabbinic commentators — chiefly Aben Ezra, Rashi (R. Solomon), Fagius, Jonathan, Onkelos, the LXX, Lyra, and Jerome — arguing points such as that the Proverbs of the New Testament derive from Jewish tradition, that lifting the hand signifies swearing an oath, and that the coveting prohibition is one
w: Targumic and Rabbinic Selections: Annotations on Exodus (Electa Thargumico-Rabbinica)

authors.aff: Professor of philosophy, then theology, at the Academy of Lausanne
authors.sig: His Metaphysica, reworked from Lausanne disputations, is an early Reformed textbook that reshapes scholastic metaphysics for theological use, arguing against Scotists, realists on universals, and the schools on essence, existence, and accident.

authors.aff: University of Leiden, professor of theology (from 1650)
authors.sig: The works here show him as exegete and polemicist: a Summa Theologiae built from Scripture, a commentary arguing Paul wrote Hebrews, and a treatise engaging Jewish responses to Christianity, with sustained argument against Socinians, Papists, and Bellarmine.
w: Consideration of Jewish Responses and Questions
Explanation of the Epistle to the Hebrews and Demonstration of Its Truth
Summa Theologica Repeated from the Scriptures

authors.aff: Minister and Professor of Sacred Theology, Illustrious Gymnasium of 's-Hertogenbosch (1656–1675); later Minister and Professor, Illustrious School of Deventer (1675–1679)
authors.sig: A representative Voetian opponent of Cartesian rationalism among the Dutch Reformed professoriate, whose Exercitationes Theologicae document the scholastic teaching of a provincial Illustrious School at the height of the Cartesio-Cocceian controversies.

authors.aff: Professor of Logic and Ethics (from 1643) and later also of Physics, University of Leiden
authors.sig: One of the earliest Dutch university professors to introduce Cartesian philosophy alongside the received Aristotelian curriculum, whose Leiden disputations transmitted an eclectic Cartesian-Aristotelian synthesis across Reformed academies in the mid-seventeenth century.

authors.aff: Professor of theology, Protestant Academy of Sedan (from 1644); minister of the Reformed Church of France
authors.sig: A leading irenic Reformed theologian of the Academy of Sedan whose Theses Theologicae offered a conciliatory, learned mapping of the doctrinal disputes dividing Catholics and Protestants.
w: Theological Theses (third edition, London 1683) — Theses Theologicae, editio tertia, London 1683
Theological Theses Defended in the Academy of Sedan (London, 1683) — one of two 1683 editions

authors.aff: Professor of theology at Utrecht (from 1644) and later Leiden (from 1654); also pastor; born in Haarlem
authors.sig: A foremost Voetian controversialist of the Dutch Further Reformation whose Summa Controversiarum gave Reformed orthodoxy a comprehensive polemical handbook against its many seventeenth-century adversaries.
w: Orations Delivered at the University of Utrecht
Summary of Religious Controversies with Infidels, Heretics, Schismatics

authors.aff: Professor of Theology, University of Utrecht (1653–1677)
authors.sig: The works held here are his Triumphus Crucis (Amsterdam, 1649), a defense of Christ's satisfaction against Socinian objections, especially those raised by Joannes Crellius against Hugo Grotius, and his Synopsis Controversiarum Theologicarum (Utrecht, 1661), a compendium of Reformed polemic arguing for the imputed righteousness of Christ and justification by Christ's obedience, directed against Crellius, the Socinians
w: Triumph of the Cross, or the Catholic Faith on the Satisfaction of the Lord

authors.aff: Synod of Dort (Dordrecht)
authors.sig: Its Acta record the Reformed response to Arminianism: election treated before reprobation, denial of freedom of the will for good after the fall, Christ's death limited to the elect, and perseverance grounded in the decree of election; the text argues extensively against the Arminians/Remonstrants.
w: Acts of the National Synod of Dort (Acta Synodi Nationalis Dordrechtanae, 1618–1619)

authors.aff: University of Utrecht — professor of metaphysics (from 1641), later professor of law; Utrecht
authors.sig: A Voetian philosopher-jurist who codified a confessionally "reformed" Aristotelian metaphysics and natural theology at Utrecht, defending scholastic orthodoxy against the rising tide of Cartesianism.

authors.aff: Minister at Plymouth and Newton St Cyres, Devon
authors.sig: His Vindiciae Gratiae Sacramentalis defends an Augustinian-Reformed doctrine of sacramental efficacy — baptism as the washing of regeneration remitting original sin in infants, succeeding circumcision as covenant sign — against Roman ex opere operato, Anabaptist objections, and bare-memorial views, arguing against Bellarmine, Zanchius, and even Calvin.
w: Vindication of Sacramental Grace (Vindiciae Gratiae Sacramentalis)
Disputations on the Satisfaction of Christ
On Our Necessary Separation from the Roman Church

authors.aff: Professor of theology, Leiden (formerly Nijmegen)
authors.sig: Wittich is the leading Dutch Reformed attempt to reconcile Descartes with Scripture; the Theologia Pacifica here shows that project applied across the loci, defending philosophical truth against Voetian critics such as Maresius.

authors.aff: Protestant Academy of Saumur (Académie de Saumur), Anjou, France; chairs of theology and Hebrew
authors.sig: The Saumur faculty defined seventeenth-century France's leading "moderate Calvinist" current—Amyraldian hypothetical universalism plus revisionist views on imputation and the Hebrew text—prompting the Reformed orthodox reaction of the Helvetic Consensus.
w: Collection of Theological Theses Disputed in the Academy of Saumur

authors.aff: Professor of theology, University of Utrecht (from 1662)
authors.sig: His Synopsis Theologiae et speciatim Oeconomiae Foederum Dei is a two-volume Reformed dogmatics organized around covenant economy, defending orthodox Christology, Scripture as the principle of theology, and Trinitarian doctrine against Papists, Socinians, Arminians, Jews, Anabaptists, and Lutherans.
w: Synopsis of Theology, especially of the Economy of the Covenants of God
Synopsis of Theology, particularly of the Economy of God's Covenants

authors.aff: Professor of theology, University of Groningen
authors.sig: His Doctrina Foederum (Amsterdam, 1688) is a full covenant-theology system of doctrine, heavily exegetical and polemical against Roman Catholics above all, but also Socinians, Arminians, Lutherans and Anabaptists.
w: Doctrine of the Covenants, or a System of Didactic Theology

authors.aff: Professor of Philosophy, Franeker (1660–1668)
authors.sig: His Institutiones Metaphysicae shows how a mid-seventeenth-century Reformed philosophy professor framed metaphysics as a discipline serving theology while resisting its reduction to theology.

authors.aff: Professor of theology and Hebrew at Duisburg, then Frankfurt an der Oder, and from 1677 at the University of Utrecht (succeeding Gisbertus Voetius)
authors.sig: A leading divine of the Dutch Further Reformation whose Theoretico-practica theologia—admired by Jonathan Edwards—became a paradigmatic synthesis of Reformed scholastic doctrine and practical piety, while his anti-Cartesian polemics defended Voetian orthodoxy.
w: The Gangrene of Cartesian Novelties, ded. William III of Orange (Novitatum Cartesianarum Gangraena)

authors.aff: Professor of theology and church history, University of Leiden; earlier professor at Heidelberg
authors.sig: A leading late-seventeenth-century Dutch Reformed theologian and church historian at Leiden whose vast erudition and controversial writings consolidated Reformed orthodoxy against its Catholic, Arminian, and Socinian opponents.

authors.aff: Pastor and professor of Greek, then theology, at Heidelberg; Palatine ecclesiastical councillor
authors.sig: The Opera Omnia gathered by J. H. Heidegger (Zurich, 1698) collects his disputations and treatises, which here defend true worship, the church, Christian liberty, Christology, Scripture, and the civil magistrate against Papists, Scholastics, Hobbes, and the Lutherans.

authors.aff: Professor of theology (and earlier of philosophy/ethics and church history) at the Carolinum, Zurich; earlier at Heidelberg and Steinfurt
authors.sig: A principal architect of late Swiss Reformed orthodoxy whose Corpus Theologiae Christianae and authorship of the Formula Consensus Helvetica made him a defining systematic and confessional voice of late seventeenth-century Calvinism.
w: The Tomb of the Council of Trent (Tumulus Concilii Tridentini)
The Tomb of the Council of Trent (Tumulus Concilii Tridentini)
The Tomb of the Council of Trent (Tumulus Tridentini Concilii)
Christian Theology for the Practice of Piety

authors.aff: Professor of divinity, University of Leiden
authors.sig: The two volumes held here are his Miscellanea Sacra: four books on Hebrew prophecy, the tabernacle, Aaron's priesthood versus Christ's, and the Sanhedrin, followed by twenty-three historical-critical exercitationes that defend traditional readings against Grotius, Spencer, and Jewish, Papist and Donatist objections.

authors.aff: Professor of theology, Utrecht (from 1678)
authors.sig: The works held here show him as a Voetian scholastic polemicist: a six-book history of Jansenism, an apology for Reformed truth aimed chiefly at Roman Catholics, and a compendium of theology following Voetius and Hoornbeeck's order.
w: On the Truth of the Reformed or Evangelical Religion
Six Books on the History of Jansenism

authors.aff: Professor of theology at the University of Frankfurt an der Oder
w: Candid Inquiry into the Controversies of the Evangelicals
Two Treatises on the Ecclesiastical Union of the Evangelicals

authors.aff: Professor of Theology and Philosophy, University of Franeker (1686–1704); Professor of Theology, University of Utrecht (1704–1718)
authors.sig: The central and most controversial figure of the 'Röellian' dispute over the proper use of reason in Reformed dogmatics, whose Cartesian-inflected rationalism provoked one of the sharpest intra-Reformed theological controversies of the early Enlightenment.

w: Examination of Two Treatises by Mr. La Placette

authors.aff: Academy of Geneva; professor of theology, Geneva
authors.sig: A leading early-eighteenth-century Genevan Reformed theologian whose systematic and ethical works helped transmit Calvinist orthodoxy in a more irenic, pastoral key across Protestant Europe.

authors.aff: Professor of theology at Franeker, Groningen, and Leiden
authors.sig: A leading Dutch Reformed dogmatician and exegete, he wrote in the didactico-elenctic mode against Papists, Socinians, Arminians, and Cocceians; the library holds his Compendium Theologiae Christianae Didactico-Elencticum and his exegetical exercises on twenty-five Old Testament passages.
w: Scriptural Exercises on Twenty-Five Selected Passages of the Old Testament

authors.aff: University of Frankfurt an der Oder (Viadrina): professor of physics and (extraordinary, later doctoral) professor of theology; earlier Reformed court preacher at Stolp (Słupsk), Pomerania
authors.sig: A late-17th/early-18th-century Reformed orthodox professor at the Viadrina in Frankfurt an der Oder whose academic disputations expound the central loci of Calvinist dogmatics.

authors.aff: University of Franeker (professor of Oriental languages, then theology, and later sacred history), Friesland
authors.sig: A leading Dutch Reformed exegete whose commentary on Isaiah and historical reconstruction of the ancient synagogue made him one of the most learned biblical scholars of the early eighteenth century.
w: Outline of Sacred History and Chronology

authors.aff: French Protestant church, Berlin
authors.sig: His Histoire du Concile de Constance, held here in two Amsterdam volumes, is a Protestant historical account of the council that condemned Hus and Wycliffe, drawing heavily on Hus, Gerson, Von der Hardt, and Niem and engaging Maimbourg's Catholic historiography.

events: Zwingli at Zurich
He begins to preach through Matthew from the pulpit of the Grossmünster.
The Marburg Colloquy
Luther and Zwingli agree on fourteen articles and part over the Lord’s Supper.
The Institutes, and Geneva
Calvin publishes the first Institutes at Basel and is kept at Geneva by Farel.
The Consensus Tigurinus
Calvin and Bullinger agree on the sacraments.
The Geneva Academy
Beza is its first rector. The French churches adopt their Confession the same year.
The Heidelberg Catechism
Frederick III brings the Palatinate into the Reformed fold.
St Bartholomew’s Day
The massacre of the Huguenots; refugees carry the faith north and east.
Leiden
William of Orange founds the university in thanks for the city’s relief from siege.
The Remonstrance
Arminius’s followers set out five articles against the Reformed doctrine of grace.
The Synod of Dort
Delegates from the Netherlands, Britain, the Palatinate, Hesse, Nassau, Bremen, Emden and the Swiss cities.
Amyraut’s Brief Treatise
Saumur’s doctrine of hypothetical universal grace opens forty years of debate.
Westphalia, and the covenant
The Reformed faith is recognized in the Empire; Cocceius publishes his Doctrine of the Covenant.
The Formula Consensus
Heidegger and Turretin draw up the last confession of the Swiss churches.
The Revocation
Louis XIV revokes the Edict of Nantes; the Huguenots scatter to the Netherlands, Prussia and England.
